text: Sea's e-commerce cost of revenue rose 38.6%, from US$5.2 billion in FY2023 to US$7.2 billion in FY2024, and this increase was primarily driven by higher logistics costs as order volume grew 33.0%, from 8.2 billion orders in 2023 to 10.9 billion orders in 2024 [Sea, FY2024, p.97]. Cost of revenue for e-commerce services generally comprises logistics and other value-added service expenses, bank transaction fees on the Shopee platform, server and hosting costs, and staff compensation and welfare costs (including share-based compensation) [Sea, FY2024, p.92-94], but the FY2024 increase was attributed specifically to the surge in order volume driving up logistics costs.

answer: Sea's e-commerce cost of revenue rose 38.6%, from US$5.2 billion in FY2023 to US$7.2 billion in FY2024, and this increase was primarily driven by higher logistics costs as order volume grew 33.0%, from 8.2 billion orders in 2023 to 10.9 billion orders in 2024 [Sea, FY2024, p.97]. Cost of revenue for e-commerce services generally comprises logistics and other value-added service expenses, bank transaction fees on the Shopee platform, server and hosting costs, and staff compensation and welfare costs (including share-based compensation) [Sea, FY2024, p.92-94], but the FY2024 increase was attributed specifically to the surge in order volume driving up logistics costs.
